gloss: imperial princess; daughter of an emperor

definitions.gloss: imperial princess; daughter of an emperor
definitions.explanation: A princess who is the daughter of an emperor or empress. Specifically refers to female members of the imperial family who are children of the reigning or past emperor.

examples.japanese: {皇女|こうじょ}が{誕生|たんじょう}した。
{平安|へいあん}{時代|じだい}の{皇女|こうじょ}は{斎宮|さいぐう}として{伊勢|いせ}{神宮|じんぐう}に{仕|つか}えることがあった。
examples.english: In the Heian period, imperial princesses sometimes served at Ise Shrine as high priestesses.

examples.japanese: {皇女|こうじょ}は{結婚|けっこん}すると{皇籍|こうせき}を{離|はな}れる。
examples.english: An imperial princess leaves the imperial family register upon marriage.

notes:
Compound of {皇|こう} ('emperor; imperial') and {女|じょ} ('daughter; woman'). The formal term for a daughter of the emperor, used in historical, legal, and news contexts.

USAGE:
- In modern Japan, {皇女|こうじょ} refers to daughters of the emperor. Under current law ({皇室典範|こうしつてんぱん}), a {皇女|こうじょ} loses her imperial status upon marrying a commoner.
- In historical contexts, {皇女|こうじょ} may also be read as ひめみこ (the native Japanese reading), especially in literature about the Heian period.
- The male counterpart is {皇子|おうじ} ('imperial prince; son of an emperor').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {皇女|こうじょ}の{誕生|たんじょう}: birth of an imperial princess
- {皇女|こうじょ}の{降嫁|こうか}: an imperial princess marrying into a non-imperial family
- {内親王|ないしんのう}・{皇女|こうじょ}: formal/informal pairing for 'imperial princess'

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {皇子|おうじ}: imperial prince — the male counterpart, a son of the emperor
- {内親王|ないしんのう}: imperial princess (formal title) — the official title granted to daughters and granddaughters of the emperor
- {王女|おうじょ}: princess — a princess of a non-imperial monarchy, or a general literary term for 'princess'
- {皇族|こうぞく}: imperial family member — the collective term for all members of the imperial household
